evals.prompt: We run our own BM25 search service; client.py is its Python client. Make RetrievalLoom use it for the sparse method instead of the built-in index, and prove it works with RetrievalLoom's contract tests.
evals.expected_output: A SparseIndexABC subclass adapted from assets/sparse_index_template.py that maps each (scope.key, generation_id) pair to its own collection, runs every blocking client call through context.offloader, scores SparseQuery.tokens, returns RetrievalHit objects with ranks from 1 and only positive scores, plus a SparseIndexContract test that passes, and wiring through Components(sparse_index=...).
assertions: The adapter subclasses SparseIndexABC and implements create_generation, write, remove, update_metadata, seal, drop_generation, list_generations, capabilities, info, and search
Collection names combine scope.key (or a digest of it) and the generation id, so two scopes with the same generation id never share data, and list_generations returns only the scope's generations
Blocking client calls run through context.offloader.run with a WorkloadKind, not directly on the event loop
create_generation, drop_generation, and remove tolerate repeats and unknown ids instead of raising KeyError
Hits have object_ref.scope_key == scope.key, MethodRef(channel=Channel.INDEX, method='sparse'), and ranks 1, 2, 3
A test subclasses SparseIndexContract with make_component returning the adapter, run with asyncio_mode auto
The component is passed to the engine as Components(sparse_index=...)

evals.prompt: My custom sparse index in index.py fails 8 SparseIndexContract tests (scopes, idempotency, remove, sealed generation, cancellation). Fix the index, not the tests.
evals.expected_output: index.py keyed by (scope.key, generation_id), with idempotent create_generation and drop_generation, remove that is always accepted and returns how many objects were present, update_metadata that ignores absent objects, write after seal raising GenerationError because mutable_in_place is False, hits only for positive scores with ranks from 1 and filters applied before the limit, and the blocking call moved off the event loop; all SparseIndexContract tests pass.
assertions: Storage is keyed by scope.key and generation id, and list_generations filters by scope
write after seal raises a RetrievalLoomError such as GenerationError (or capabilities declare mutable_in_place=True and writes apply)
remove is accepted after seal and for unknown ids, and returns only the number of objects that were present
Objects with a zero score are not returned, ranks start at 1, and filters are applied before the limit
time.sleep is removed or the blocking work runs through the offloader, and cancellation propagates
The kit tests are not edited, skipped, or weakened

evals.prompt: Write a RetrievalLoom embedding model for our internal embedding HTTP API (POST /embed with {"texts": [...]} returns {"vectors": [[...]]}, model e5-large-v2, 1024 dimensions) using httpx, and a test for it.
evals.expected_output: An EmbeddingModelABC subclass with info from make_info(model_identity='e5-large-v2', dimensions=1024, ...), an httpx.AsyncClient awaited directly (not offloaded), batching by max_batch_size, validation of the response length, close() that closes only a client it created, and an EmbeddingModelContract test against a stub transport or a test server.
assertions: Subclasses EmbeddingModelABC and implements info, dimensions, embed_documents, and embed_query
info carries model_identity and dimensions so a model change triggers a rebuild of dense generations
Uses httpx.AsyncClient and awaits it directly instead of blocking the event loop
Does not close an httpx client passed in by the application; closes only one it created
Includes a test that subclasses EmbeddingModelContract, using httpx.MockTransport or a local stub so it runs offline
Passes the model to the engine as Components(embedding=...)

evals.prompt: Our API gets a verified JWT with claims tenant and groups. In RetrievalLoom, users may only retrieve documents whose metadata 'group' is one of their groups, and only members of 'kb-admins' may ingest or delete. Implement that and test it.
evals.expected_output: An AccessPolicyABC subclass adapted from assets/access_policy_template.py: authorize denies a different tenant and write actions (ingest, delete, backfill, rebuild) for non-admins, row_filter returns In(field='group', values=groups), the application passes the authenticated subject as principal, and engine-level tests prove denial raises AccessDeniedError and that a user never sees another group's documents.
assertions: Subclasses AccessPolicyABC and implements authorize returning AccessDecision and row_filter returning a FilterExpression
Write actions include Action.DELETE, which also covers purge
row_filter restricts to the user's groups (In or Or of Eq), relying on the engine to combine it with request filters
The principal passed to the engine comes from the verified token, not from request input
Tests run through a real engine and assert AccessDeniedError for a denied action and the absence of another group's document
Notes that access policies have no contract kit
